title: Ephemeral client-side policy DSL — sketch & tradeoffs
content:
Goal:
- Design a tiny, ephemeral client-side policy language (DSL) carried with each request that encodes routing/caching/quality hints for inference edge proxies and the serving runtime.
- Must be small, human-readable for debugging, and actionable by gateways without heavy parsing cost.
- Primary user: mobile/web client SDK + edge proxies + self-hosted gateway.

Constraints and non-goals:
- NOT an authorization language. Secrets/permissions handled upstream.
- NOT a replacement for long-lived server-side policies. This is per-request hints only.
- Size budget: <= 256 bytes when base64 encoded into header. Prefer <160 bytes.
- Backwards compatibility: runtime must ignore unknown keys.

Design principles (tradeoffs):
- Simplicity over full expressivity — prefer a compact key:value set rather than recursive AST.
- Explicit fallbacks — servers must document default behavior when hint absent.
- Wire-friendly — JSON-like but terser. Consider k=v pairs separated by commas.
- Allow sampling directives for telemetry (so we can enable evals/test traces without changing SDK).

Proto grammar (informal):
- format: v1;k1=v1;k2=v2;...
- keys whitelisted: r (route preference), q (quality-level), b (batching hint), c (cache-mode), t (ttl-ms), s (sample-id), m (model-preference), f (fallback-policy)
- example: v1;r=region:eu;q=fast,b=1;c=soft;t=120000;s=exp-42

Key semantics (notes):
- r (route preference): string; values: region:<short>, tier:<prod|canary|fallback>, node:<id>. E.g., region:us-west. Server uses as ranking signal; cannot force route.
- q (quality-level): enum { best, balanced, fast, economize }. Maps to model selection + decoding params. 'best' increases max tokens and decoding beams; 'economize' suggests aggressive quantization/low-temp, smaller model.
- b (batching hint): integer; priority for batching. 0 = prefer immediate, 1 = allow short batching (50ms), 2 = allow longer batching (200ms). Server respects latency SLOs first.
- c (cache-mode): {none, soft, require}. 'soft' allows cache lookups but not mandatory; 'require' means best-effort fallback to cached response only. Include warning: 'require' must not expose privacy data.
- t (ttl-ms): numeric; TTL for caching of generated response. Only valid if c != none.
- s (sample-id): arbitrary string used to tag for trace/qa purposes. Should be rate-limited on client side.
- m (model-preference): short model tag or family. 'm=gpt-xyz-q4' note that server may override for capacity/security reasons.
- f (fallback-policy): {downscale, degrade, error}. 'downscale' means pick a lower-capacity model; 'degrade' means return partial result; 'error' forces immediate 503 if preferred constraints can't be met.

Header/transport: 
- Header name: X-RW-Client-Policy (string). For SDKs we will also accept ?policy=base64 in query for convenience but discourage for GETs.
- Encoding: UTF-8; if header length > 180 bytes or contains special chars, client must base64 encode and set header X-RW-Client-Policy-Base64: true. Server should log length for telemetry.

Example header raw: 
X-RW-Client-Policy: v1;r=region:eu;q=balanced;b=1;c=soft;t=60000;s=test-123

Mini-spec: Routing decision flow (server-side):
1. Authorization & schema validation (fast parse): if header missing -> defaults.
2. Apply hints as ranking signals (r, m, q). If 'f=error' and none of constraints satisfiable, return 503.
3. Batching decisions consult 'b' but obey server latency SLO.
4. Caching: if c=require and cache miss -> behavior per 'f'. If c=soft, act as advisory.
5. Observability: tag traces with sample-id (s) and hint vector.

ASCII diagram (client -> edge -> control plane -> runtime):
[App SDK] -- X-RW-Client-Policy --> [Edge Proxy] -- hints+request ---> [Control Plane Router] -- routed --> [Serving Runtime]
Edge Proxy acts as a fast filter, can mutate small fields (e.g., downgrade q from best->balanced when on metered mobile). Control plane has final say.

API shape for sdk->edge (JSON example for SDK debugging/console):
{ "policy": "v1;r=region:eu;q=balanced;b=1;c=soft;t=60000;s=test-123" }
(note: this JSON only used internally in SDK debug UI; wire prefers header format)

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: embedding any user-identifying info in s/sample-id could leak PII into traces. Need an SDK-level hashing guideline.
- Pressure on heuristics: clients may overuse 'best' and cause spikes. Need quotas or score-based admission.
- Complexity for proxies: too many keys means we must maintain compatibility table. Keep key set small.
- Attack surface: 'f=error' could be abused to cause denial conditions. Probably disable 'error' for public clients and mark as enterprise-only.

Tests & rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal canary only. SDK adds opt-in flag. Gate header parsing with feature flag.
- Phase 1: sampling rollout (s=) tied to ENG-1267; 1% of traffic annotated. Collect telemetry on key usage and header lengths.
- Phase 2: allow 'q' and 'b' as advisory for all OSS SDKs.
- Phase 3: add per-team policy registry (server-side canonicalization) and telemetry dashboards.

Telemetry to collect (minimal):
- header_present (bool), header_size_bytes, keys_used[], sample_id_frequency, action_taken_for_policy (mapped decision), dropped_due_to_security

Implementation notes (todo):
- Edge proxy: tiny parser util written in Rust + C++ for envoy lua filter fallback. Keep zero-allocation parse for common path.
- SDKs: add convicting API: PolicyBuilder with fluent helpers. Default to empty policy.
- Control plane: define admission scoring that maps q/b/c -> numeric score for route selection.

Action items (me):
- Draft proto parsing util and microbenchmark (Marcus).
- Add feature flag + telemetry pipeline stub (Eleanor).
- Write SDK builder PR doc (Priya).
- Put a note in Confluence with examples and security checklist.

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep header name short and unique. X-RW-Client-Policy seems fine, avoids X-Forwarded-* confusion.
- Consider signed policies for privileged clients (enterprise) so proxies can trust fields like f=error. But that smells like auth.
- When in doubt, prefer advisory semantics. Only enterprise/backed clients can require hard behaviors.

Scratch rough API surface for PolicyBuilder (JS):
- new PolicyBuilder().region('eu').quality('balanced').batchHint(1).cacheSoft(60000).sample('exp-42').toHeader()
- toHeader() returns the string ready to put into X-RW-Client-Policy (handles base64 decision)

Unresolved UX: how do we expose this to third-party integrators without encouraging misuse? Maybe an "honor system" plus quotas and server-side overrides.

End of sketch.
